## F1 — service_ext_paid_ro_points: "paid in full" rule counts every charge; compute drops deductible rows (XF B.8/B.9)
- Rule (Y:1076, also baseline.rule Y:1275, compute_basis ro_balance/paid_in_full Y:1153-1154): "The paid repair order is paid in full when its charges, less every credit on it, less the payments received on it, plus any payment returned on it, come to zero or less, and a repair order not paid in full earns no points."
- Compute (Y:1109-1113): `ro_balance` = diagnostic fees + `paid_labor` + `paid_parts` + shop fees + returned payments - every credit - every payment, where `paid_labor`/`paid_parts` filter `pay_type='customer_pay'`.
- Records hold other charges on the same RO: B:646 (service_evt_labor_pricing) "A deductible owed on covered work is posted as a labor row with pay_type service_contract_deductible or warranty_deductible, 0.0 hours and the deductible amount"; db_schema pay_type enum = customer_pay | service_contract_deductible | warranty_deductible.
- Witness: paid RO with customer-pay labor 200.00 (line A) and a service-contract deductible labor row 100.00 (line B), payments 200.00. Rule: charges 300.00 less 200.00 = 100.00 > 0, not paid in full, 0 points. Compute: 200.00 less 200.00 = 0, paid in full, points credited. The rule's "its charges" and compute disagree whenever a deductible on the RO is unpaid.
- Fix direction (authoring side): either add the deductible rows (labor and parts, pay_type service_contract_deductible / warranty_deductible) to `ro_balance`, or narrow the rule sentence to name exactly the charges compute sums (diagnostic fees, customer-pay labor and parts, shop fees).

## F2 — service_ext_early_payment_discount: same "paid in full" mismatch (XF B.8/B.9)
- Rule (Y:2027, baseline.rule Y:2220, compute_basis invoice_balance Y:2201): "The invoice is paid in full when its charges, less every credit on it, less the payments received on it, plus any payment returned on it, come to zero or less."
- Compute (Y:2056-2061, used by discount_due Y:2076): `invoice_balance` uses `invoice_labor`/`invoice_parts` filtered to `pay_type='customer_pay'`, so a deductible labor/parts row on the fleet invoice is not a charge in compute but is one of "its charges" in the rule. Same witness as F1 flips the discount from 0 (rule) to a positive credit (compute).

## F3 — service_ext_comeback_labor_credit: "the repeat labor charge" is singular in the rule; compute sums every customer-pay labor row of the paid RO (XF B.8/B.9, second-record decoy)
- Rule (Y:1788; baseline.rule Y:1955; compute_basis paid_ro/repeat_labor Y:1925-1926): "the paid repair order is the repair order of the latest payment received on the account, the repeat labor charge is its customer-pay labor charge, and the unit is the vehicle on that charge." Also "The credit basis is the repeat labor charge.", "the repeat labor charge's line date", "On any other account the credit is the repeat labor charge times comeback_labor_covered_pct", "The comeback credit is booked against the repeat labor charge as credit_reason comeback_repair."
- Compute (Y:1799): `repeat_labor: SUM('service_ro_lines', 'amount', event_type='service_labor_charged', pay_type='customer_pay', repair_order_number=paid_ro)` — every customer-pay labor row on every concern line of the paid RO; `repeat_date`/`repeat_odometer`/`repeat_store` (Y:1802-1803, 1813) take the LATEST such row.
- Witness: paid RO with line A (the repeat, labor 300.00) and line B (an unrelated customer-pay job, labor 150.00), non-fleet account, in warranty, comeback_labor_covered_pct 1.0. Compute credits 450.00; the rule's singular "its customer-pay labor charge" gives no reading that yields 450.00 (a reader picks one charge, 300.00 or 150.00, or cannot decide), and "booked against the repeat labor charge" names no single row for `source_line_id`/`line_letter`. Same singular-booking gap in service_ext_early_payment_discount (Y:2027): "The discount is booked against the invoice's labor charge as credit_reason early_payment_discount." while the amount reads all of "the invoice's customer-pay labor ... charges" — which labor row carries the credit is undetermined when the invoice has two or more labor rows.
- Fix direction: state in the rule that the repeat labor charge is the total of the paid RO's customer-pay labor charges (and which row the credit is booked against), or key the read to one row (e.g. the latest customer-pay labor charge) in compute.

- `months_open: MONTHS(F('opened_date'), NOW)` (Y:1567) is a binding of factor `tenure_point_value` (bindings Y:1608-1610: months_open, point_value).

- Fix direction: give held_points_rule its own account-age binding (or make months_open a plain non-factor binding that both factors read).
